Mission

"Rising Promise closes the opportunity gap by providing career-focused training, advanced education, and holistic support to underserved communities. We build pathways to economic independence that strengthen families, create generational wealth, and empower the next generation of leaders."

Vision
Community Over Circumstance

To build communities where opportunity, housing, and career pathways create generational stability — where a person's zip code does not define their ceiling.

Strategic Positioning
Not a Startup. An Ecosystem.

Rising Promise operates with the footprint of a fully built multi-state nonprofit from day one — enabled by a 3-entity contracting and grant ecosystem designed to capture multiple funding lanes simultaneously.

Case for Support
Why Rising Promise Exists Now

The Problem

The national assisted living staffing shortage is critical. Transitional housing demand is at historic highs. Underserved adults — women in crisis, veterans, returning citizens, foster youth — have no structured on-ramp to living-wage careers.

The Solution

Rising Promise trains workers, places them in real jobs, stabilizes their housing, and supports employer partners — all within a single infrastructure. Our model turns community need into a self-sustaining workforce and housing pipeline.

The Advantage

Three legally distinct entities. SAM.gov registered. Website and donation infrastructure live. A CFRE-level development advisor on board. Rising Promise is positioned to receive and deploy funds from day one of 501(c)(3) approval.

Section 02

3-Entity Power Structure

The framework enabling Rising Promise to capture grants, federal contracts, and housing revenue simultaneously.

The Strategic Advantage

Most nonprofits operate in a single funding lane. Rising Promise runs three legally distinct entities — each with its own revenue strategy — allowing simultaneous pursuit of foundation grants, federal contracts, earned revenue, and real estate commissions. To funders and government agencies, this reads as a fully operational multi-state organization from day one.

Entity 01 — Primary
Rising Promise
Texas Nonprofit CAGE Pending

  • Healthcare workforce funding
  • Housing & education grants
  • WIOA eligible training provider
  • 501(c)(3) determination pending
Entity 02 — Operations
Grey Taurus LLC
Florida LLC CAGE Secured

Role: Operations & Contracting Engine

  • Federal subcontracting
  • Staffing & admin services
  • ALF operations management
  • Management services agreements
  • SAM.gov registered
Entity 03 — Affiliate
Waite & Associates
NY Licensed Broker CAGE Secured

Role: Housing Affiliate

  • Adds multi-state geographic footprint
  • Property sourcing support
  • Real estate referrals when active

  • SAM.gov registered · credential value
Entity Separation — Non-Negotiable
Rising Promise (nonprofit) and Grey Taurus LLC (for-profit) funds must never commingle. All payments between entities require a signed Management Services Agreement or Teaming Agreement. Jason's personal funds used for org expenses must be documented as founder loans or reimbursements. Violation risks 501(c)(3) status.

Section 04

Program Architecture

Programs ordered by priority. Fundraising unlocks everything. Programs 2 and 3 require audit and completion funds before launch can be planned.

Priority Logic
No program launches without funding. Priority 1 is grant capture and donor activation. Programs 2 and 3 are both unverified in completion status — they need auditing and budget planning before any launch timeline can be set. No assumptions made on "70% done."
01
Fundraising & Grant Activation
Priority 1 · Immediate
▼

Everything else is downstream from this. No staff. No clinicals. No housing operations without cash. The 90-day goal is to get the CFRE activated, 5 Tier 1 grants submitted, CRA bank pitches in motion, and the raffle live. Target: first $50K–$100K within 60 days.

Key actions: Activate CFRE this week · Submit 5 Tier 1 grant applications · Pitch 3 local banks for CRA funds · Launch raffle once prize and sponsor confirmed · Candid profile Bronze Seal · Relay Financial account opened.

02
Heart of Healthcare — CNA Certification
Pending Audit + Completion Funding
▼

Fast-track CNA certification. Hybrid online + in-person clinical. Completion status of existing platform is unverified — requires a full audit of what exists, what works, and what budget is needed to complete. Launch timeline cannot be set until audit is done and funds are secured.

When ready: WIOA vouchers $7,500–$8,500/student. Register on FL ETPL post-501(c)(3) to unlock state funding. Clinical site partnership required (can use Grey Taurus ALF when operational).

Target population: Women in crisis, veterans, career-changers, foster youth 18–24, returning citizens.

03
Pathways in Technology — CompTIA IT
Pending Audit + Completion Funding
▼

CompTIA A+, Network+, Security+ certification track. Platform partially built. Completion status unverified — requires the same audit and budget planning process as CNA before any launch can be considered. Strong WIOA alignment when ready.

No action required until CNA program is funded, audited, and in launch planning. These two programs may share infrastructure and budget planning once audits are complete.

Section 05

ALF / Housing Pipeline

Option A takeover strategy, startup cost model, and the Grey Taurus operating framework.

Option A: The CHOW Takeover Strategy

Instead of building from scratch ($500K+, 9–14 months), Grey Taurus identifies existing licensed ALF shells via the AHCA Closed Provider database, negotiates a lease from struggling or retiring operators, and files a Change of Ownership (CHOW) application. Target: operational within 2–4 weeks of lease execution. Rising Promise trains the staff. Grey Taurus operates the house.

Where to Find Option A Facilities
Lead Sources

Online Phase · Launch Name
V.I.A. — Vanguard Innovation Academy

"Via" is Latin for The Way — The Path. Modern, tech-forward identity for the online-first PEP scholarship learning center model.

Format: Learning Center for registered homeschoolers. Gamified AI-driven curriculum mapped to Florida B.E.S.T. standards with unconventional elite subject names.

Physical School · Future Name
NOBLE Institute

Network of Black Leaders & Entrepreneurs. Reclaims "Nobility" for underrepresented communities. The Robin Hood model flagship — premium tuition funds Heritage Tier (PEP-only) seats at no out-of-pocket cost.

Copy: "A Noble path to a global legacy." Transitions from V.I.A. when a physical location is secured and diploma-granting status is earned.

Kenya Roberts, CFRE

Section 17 · Grant-Ready

Theory of Change

Required by Tier 2 funders. Describes the logical path from inputs to long-term impact. Pull the summary paragraph directly into grant narratives.

The Core Premise

People do not lack potential — they lack access. When underserved individuals are given the right combination of training, housing stability, and support, they achieve economic independence. Rising Promise builds the entire pathway, not just one piece of it.

Inputs
Grants & donations
Leadership team

Systemic equity
Assumptions
What Must Be True
  • Participants are motivated when real pathways are made accessible
  • Employer demand for trained healthcare and IT workers remains strong
  • Housing stability is a prerequisite for sustained employment
  • Wraparound support reduces dropout and incompletion
  • 3-entity structure sustains funding beyond any single source
How We Measure It
Key Metrics
  • Program completion rate — target 80%+
  • Certification pass rate — target 75%+
  • Employment placement within 90 days — target 70%+
  • Housing stability at 6 months — target 85%+
  • Average wage at placement vs. prior earnings
  • Employer partner retention rate
Pull This Paragraph Directly Into Grant Narratives
Theory of Change — Summary
"Rising Promise operates on the premise that economic instability is a structural problem, not a personal failing. By integrating career-focused certification training, transitional housing placement, and wraparound case management into a single coordinated model, we create the conditions under which individuals move from economic vulnerability to self-sufficiency. Our inputs — credentialed staff, clinical partnerships, government-aligned training programs, and a multi-entity operational ecosystem — generate activities that produce certified, employed, and housed graduates. In the short term, participants achieve living-wage employment and housing stability. In the long term, families break cycles of poverty, communities gain skilled workers, and underserved populations build generational economic equity. We do not offer programs in isolation. We build pathways."

Jason Pilgrim is the Founder and Executive Director of Rising Promise, a Texas-based 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to closing the opportunity gap through career training, transitional housing, and wraparound support services. With more than 15 years of experience across environmental services, construction, logistics, and business development, Jason brings rare operational depth and mission-driven vision to the organization.

He built Rising Promise on a fundamental conviction: that access to opportunity — not circumstance of birth — should define a person's future. Jason architected the organization's three-entity ecosystem, securing SAM.gov registration and CAGE certification to position Rising Promise for federal contracting and foundation grant funding simultaneously.
"I've spent my life building things — businesses, systems, solutions. But the most important thing I've ever built is opportunity for people who were told they didn't deserve one."
Jason Pilgrim is the Founder and Executive Director of Rising Promise, a multi-state 501(c)(3) nonprofit operating at the intersection of workforce development, transitional housing, and advanced education for underserved communities. His career spans more than 15 years across environmental science services, construction management, logistics operations, and entrepreneurial business development — building and scaling complex operational systems in high-stakes environments.

Jason's path to nonprofit leadership was shaped by a lifelong observation: that structural barriers, not lack of ambition, determine outcomes for millions of Americans. Growing up with an entrepreneurial spirit but without the resources, networks, or mentorship that could have accelerated his journey, he channeled that lived experience into building the infrastructure he wished had existed — first for himself, and now for others.

At Rising Promise, Jason designed the organization's unique three-entity federal contracting and grant ecosystem — combining Rising Promise's nonprofit grant eligibility, Grey Taurus LLC's operational and subcontracting capacity, and Waite & Associates' real estate affiliate network. This structure enables the organization to pursue federal contracts, foundation grants, and program-generated revenue simultaneously, operating with the footprint of a fully established multi-state organization from day one.

Jason oversees organizational strategy, government contract development, program architecture, and all executive partnerships. He is the primary relationship holder for federal agencies, workforce boards, and institutional funders, and serves as the operational and visionary backbone of the Rising Promise mission.
"I've spent my life building things — businesses, systems, solutions. But the most important thing I've ever built is opportunity for people who were told they didn't deserve one."
Leadership Bio

Shawn J. Wright, FNP

Program Director — Rising Promise

SW
Shawn J. Wright, FNP
Program Director
Family Nurse Practitioner · Clinical Compliance
Shawn J. Wright is a licensed Family Nurse Practitioner and the Program Director of Rising Promise, providing clinical leadership and healthcare compliance oversight for the organization's workforce training initiatives. With advanced nursing credentials and direct experience in long-term care settings, Shawn serves as the qualified Program Director for Rising Promise's CNA certification track — meeting Texas HHSC NATCEP requirements for nurse aide training program approval.

His role spans curriculum oversight, clinical site coordination, instructor credentialing, and student competency evaluation. He ensures Rising Promise's healthcare programs meet all state and federal standards while remaining accessible to students without prior healthcare backgrounds — including women in crisis, veterans, and career-changers seeking stable, living-wage employment.
"I became a nurse because I wanted to help people heal. Now I help them build futures."
Shawn J. Wright is a licensed Family Nurse Practitioner (FNP) and the Program Director of Rising Promise. As an FNP — combining RN licensure with a Master of Science in Nursing and advanced clinical training — Shawn exceeds Texas HHSC requirements for NATCEP Program Director designation, which requires a minimum of two years of nursing experience including at least one year in long-term care. His credentials position Rising Promise for immediate state CNA program approval and WIOA Eligible Training Provider status upon application.

Shawn's responsibilities at Rising Promise include oversight of the CNA certification curriculum, coordination with clinical site partners, supervision of contracted instructors and skills verification staff, and final sign-off on student competency evaluations. He plays a central role in ensuring clinical integrity while maintaining accessibility — designing pathways that welcome students with no prior healthcare background.

Beyond his clinical role, Shawn is a mission-aligned leader whose belief in healthcare as a vehicle for economic mobility drives Rising Promise's program philosophy. He works closely with the Executive Director and Finance Director to ensure program delivery remains both compliant and financially sustainable as the organization scales its healthcare workforce pipeline.
"I became a nurse because I wanted to help people heal. Now I help them build futures."

Melissa Meeham, MPA

Finance & Administration Director — Rising Promise

MM
Melissa Meeham, MPA
Finance & Administration Director
Master of Public Administration · 20+ yrs accounting
Melissa Meeham is the Finance and Administration Director of Rising Promise, bringing more than 20 years of experience in accounting and public administration to the organization's financial infrastructure. She holds a Master of Public Administration (MPA) and has dedicated her career to building transparent, compliant financial systems for mission-driven organizations.

At Rising Promise, Melissa oversees all financial controls, regulatory compliance, grant fund accounting, and administrative operations. Her public administration background makes her uniquely suited to nonprofit financial management — she understands the intersection of government funding requirements, fund accounting principles, and the reporting obligations that accompany federal and foundation grants.
"Sound financial management isn't just about numbers — it's about making sure every dollar reaches the people who need it most."
Melissa Meeham is the Finance and Administration Director of Rising Promise. With more than two decades of experience in accounting and public administration, and a Master of Public Administration (MPA), Melissa brings institutional-grade financial discipline to an organization built for rapid, mission-driven growth.

Melissa's background spans both private sector accounting and public administration — a combination that positions her as an exceptional steward of Rising Promise's nonprofit financial infrastructure. She is deeply familiar with fund accounting, grant compliance reporting, restricted and unrestricted fund segregation, and the financial documentation requirements of federal and state funding agencies. Her MPA training provides direct fluency in government procurement standards and the regulatory landscape governing 501(c)(3) operations.

At Rising Promise, Melissa establishes and maintains all financial controls, manages the chart of accounts, oversees annual budget development, and ensures timely filing of all tax and regulatory documents — including IRS Form 990, state charitable registrations, and federal contract reporting. She serves as primary contact for all auditors and grant compliance officers.
"Sound financial management isn't just about numbers — it's about making sure every dollar reaches the people who need it most."
Leadership Bio

Kenya Roberts, CFRE

Development & Fundraising Director — Rising Promise

KR
Kenya Roberts, CFRE
Development & Fundraising Director
Certified Fund Raising Executive
Kenya Roberts is the Development and Fundraising Director of Rising Promise and a Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) — one of the most rigorous credentials in the nonprofit sector, requiring demonstrated years of professional fundraising experience and a proven track record of results. Over her career, Kenya has raised millions of dollars for workforce development, community services, and social impact organizations.

At Rising Promise, Kenya leads all fundraising strategy, grant pipeline development, foundation relationship cultivation, and corporate sponsorship. She operates at the strategic level, directing the organization's funding architecture while leveraging AI-assisted grant drafting tools to maximize application volume and quality.
"The most powerful grant application is one where the mission speaks so clearly that the funder sees themselves in the work."
Kenya Roberts is the Development and Fundraising Director of Rising Promise and holds the Certified Fund Raising Executive (CFRE) designation — an internationally recognized credential awarded by CFRE International that requires a minimum of five years of professional fundraising experience, demonstrated results, adherence to a strict code of ethics, and successful completion of a comprehensive examination. Kenya has earned this credential through a career defined by measurable impact, having raised millions of dollars for organizations working in workforce development, community health, housing, and social services.

Kenya joined Rising Promise as a mission-aligned leader who recognized the organization's potential to address a genuine gap in workforce training and housing support for underserved populations. As Development and Fundraising Director, she is responsible for the full spectrum of Rising Promise's revenue development strategy — including foundation grant prospecting, corporate sponsor cultivation, major donor identification and stewardship, government funding strategy, and public fundraising campaign design and execution.

Kenya's approach is strategic rather than tactical. She directs funding strategy, selects targets, refines organizational positioning, and applies her funder relationships to ensure Rising Promise's proposals land with the right message in front of the right decision-makers. Her presence at the founding stage gives Rising Promise a fundraising infrastructure most peer organizations spend five to ten years building.
"The most powerful grant application is one where the mission speaks so clearly that the funder sees themselves in the work."
